items.title: Show HN: WhatsApp MCP running free on Cloudflare
items.author: zoozla
items.text:
I wanted my humble Claude on mobile to access my WhatsApp messages but the only options I could find either required WhatsApp Business or an actual server to run Baileys on.

I wanted to run it for free on ClaudeFlare and with my personal WhatsApp account, so I built this.

Important feature - it connects to your Google account as well as WhatsApp to grab the names of all your WhatsApp contacts, otherwise you get only phone numbers for many of them and search doesn't work properly.

This is a single user install because it's both gray area and very private - so point your agent at the repo and let it set things up.

items.title: Show HN: The Zelda timeline to catch up before the Ocarina of Time remake
items.author: jsomau
items.text:
I made this ahead of the Ocarina of Time remake which comes out in 17 days. I remember the feeling of playing it as a kid but I hadn’t kept up with the story so I built a timeline to catch up before the Door of Time reopens.

Nintendo’s own timeline is the authority here (Hyrule Historia and their chronicle page). The fun part was rethinking how to visualize it. It branches at the end of Ocarina into three eras depending on whether Link wins or loses, so each era is its own thread on the cloth. The threads meet again much later with Breath of the Wild.

I had a lot of help from Claude. I’d often thought about building things like this but never found the time between the day job and the rest of life.

items.title: Show HN: Esp32sim – Run ESP32 firmware in the browser
items.author: joakimeriksson
items.text:
Hi HN,

I’ve been working on esp32sim, an open-source ESP32 emulator that runs in the browser.

The fun part of the demo is that there is no ESP32 involved — the firmware is executing in the emulator.

The goal is to make ESP32 software easier to experiment with, test and simulate without always needing physical hardware connected.

Source: https://github.com/mikroverk/esp32sim

I made a short video showing it in action: https://youtu.be/waoWFilTWEc

I’m particularly interested in feedback from embedded developers: what would an emulator like this need to support before you’d actually use it for development, testing or CI?

items.title: Show HN: Pi-cowboy – use Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode as subagents
items.author: suoloordi
items.text:
pi-cowboy is an agent orchestrator for Pi(https://pi.dev) and Herdr(https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr). Break large jobs into focused subtasks, hand them off to background agents running in parallel, and consolidate the results when they finish. Each agent runs in an isolated copy-on-write Git work-tree, minimising disk overhead.

pi-cowboy can orchestrate foreign harnesses too, including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and more.

Feature highlights:

- Foreign harnesses: pi-cowboy agents can run in Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pig and Pi-Bolt, as well as Pi. This gives you great flexibility in choosing how to spend your tokens. Running out of Codex usage? Switch your pi-cowboy harness to OpenCode, select one of its free models, and let it handle the rest. Pig and Pi-Bolt are pi variants that are more efficient, with a lower memory footprint and faster performance than pi. Because pi-cowboy is designed to run multiple agents in parallel, having a lower per-agent footprint is crucial. It prevents your machine from running out of resources and lets you have higher concurrency without choking your system.

- Concurrency limits: You can configure concurrency limits at every level. Running a local model with limited resources? If a simple task already takes hours to complete, the last thing you want is to overload your machine by running too many of them at once. Set concurrency limits for that model specifically to keep resource usage under control.

You can install it on Pi as a package:

  pi install npm:pi-cowboy #(requires `herdr` 0.8+)

items.title: Show HN: Things to Do API
items.author: invalidmonk
items.text:
I built an api/mcp for local events: pop-ups, one-off events, concerts, etc. currently covering the SF bay area.

I've been building a bunch of consumer apps lately around personalization and recommendation and have had a hard time finding this data in one spot. agents can find useful stuff through tool calls / web search, but slow.

you can scrape on demand too, but i wanted a faster data set and couldn't find an existing provider for the mix of event types I was searching for.

the methodology for it is to find influential accounts/posters/etc. and do a fan out across things that they co-post with.

mcp: `claude mcp add --transport http thingstodo https://api.thingstodoapi.com/mcp`

I'm considering adding other cities. If you're building something that needs local event data, would something like this be useful and where would you want coverage?
